# task-8199b524: collinear gap bridging (partially understood)

This task has a variable background and marker color. Demonstrations introduce color 2 in selected background cells between collinear marker runs/objects. Do not assume a fixed background/marker palette. Exact selection is not fully characterized: demo layouts vary and some aligned empty gaps remain unchanged. Re-extract the geometry from all available demonstrations for each instance.

## Confirmed accepted instance

Test had an 8×29 grid, background 6 and foreground 9. The accepted output preserved the grid except these 16 coordinates (0-based row,column), all changed from 6 to 2:

- row 2: columns 13, 20, 21, 22
- row 5: columns 7, 11, 13, 15, 21, 24, 25
- row 7: columns 2, 12, 13, 14, 17, 23

No cells in rows 3, 4, or 6 changed, despite long near-horizontal cavities and apparent vertical alignments. Broad rules to fill all collinear intervals between foreground pixels/components were incorrect. Do not fill large cavity spans between parallel frame walls or automatically fill every vertical alignment.

The accepted cells are short horizontal gaps between neighboring foreground runs/features. The maximum gap length in the accepted test was three cells. This suggests selected short bridges between horizontal marker-run fragments, while other demonstrations show vertical bridges too; orientation/selection depends on the instance's geometric organization.

## Additional fresh-instance evidence (8 demos, unresolved)

A later instance used background 5, marker 0, and output fill 2. Test grid (12x14) had marker coordinates:
- r2 c4..9 (horizontal bar)
- vertical marker columns c3 at r4,6,8,9,11 and c9 at r4..9 plus r11

Most notably, demo 7 (bg3/marker8) had a horizontal run at r6 c0,c1,c3,c6,c8, plus sparse isolated markers; output filled gaps r6 c2,c4,c5,c7 and vertical selective positions on c0 and c8. Demo 8 (bg5/marker8) had top-row markers c1,c6,c9,c13,c14 and bottom row c1,c2,c5,c6,c9..14; output filled horizontal gaps between run fragments (top c2-5, c7-8, c10-12; bottom c3-4,c7-8), and selective vertical cells on columns 1 and 14 only. Vertical outputs are selective, not all aligned intervals.

The test was ultimately unsolved after 8 wrong submissions. Tried and rejected: filling all adjacent-neighbor cells; filling all row/column intervals; filling only short intervals up to 3/4 gaps; a few guessed vertical gaps; and broad gap-fill including long interior spans. Do NOT treat any of these as validated.

Tentative salient clue: Demo 7 and 8 strongly highlight horizontal gaps between marker fragments on the outermost fully featured rows (often rows containing several separated short runs). Also output has vertical fills in selected marker columns/lanes, potentially based on boundary rays / endpoints and specific component context. Test horizontal feature rows r2 (one continuous run) and r11 (two separated runs with one-cell gap c8); the likely certain horizontal addition is c8 on r11, but earlier candidates including/excluding that cell were rejected in combination with other guessed vertical changes. Preserve this as unresolved, not a solved selector.

## Demonstration evidence and pitfalls

- Eight demonstrations used varied backgrounds/foregrounds (6/9, 7/9, 3/8, 1/6, 7/5, 1/9, 6/1, 5/3). New cells were generally color 2.

- Eight demonstrations used varied backgrounds/foregrounds (6/9, 7/9, 3/8, 1/6, 7/5, 1/9, 6/1, 5/3). New cells were generally color 2.
- Demos show 2 filling gaps between separated collinear marker runs; both horizontal and vertical examples occur. Some gaps extend multiple cells (one demo had a horizontal gap around seven cells), while large frame-like cavities stayed untouched.
- Avoid a simplistic all-rows/all-columns nearest-pixel fill. Broad candidates that filled long spans between opposite frame sides and bridged every vertical alignment were rejected.
- Treat unchanged analogues as crucial. Distinguish a true gap between separate short runs from an enclosed cavity, continuous line/object, or coincidental alignment. If a plausible rule is inconsistent across demos, use remaining demo budget to discriminate rather than submitting broad fills.

## Confirmed rule from accepted fresh instance (2026)

A fresh instance was solved after two failed hypotheses and one demo: identify the bounding box of all marker-color cells, then fill background cells with color 2 only on the four sides of that bounding box. Preserve existing marker cells and everything inside/outside the perimeter. Equivalently, on the min/max marker rows fill between the leftmost/rightmost marker; on the min/max marker columns fill between the topmost/bottommost marker. Do not fill other aligned gaps, even if they have marker endpoints.

### Additional accepted test (2026)

An 18×12 test with background 7 and marker 9 was solved with zero wrong attempts. Marker bounding box (0-based) was rows 8–13, columns 3–11. Output color 2 filled exactly the previously-background cells on its perimeter:
- top row r8: c4, c9–10
- bottom row r13: c4–6, c8
- left side c3: r9, r11–12
- right side c11: r9–11
Existing 9s and all non-perimeter cells were unchanged. This independently confirms the global marker-bbox perimeter rule; fill color remains 2 even though the background/marker colors differ.

The accepted test had background 1, markers 0, output color 2, and marker bounding box rows 1–11, columns 1–12 (0-based). Successful additions were:
- row 1: columns 4, 6, 10, 11
- row 11: columns 3, 4, 10
- column 1: rows 5, 6, 8
- column 12: rows 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9
All other cells stayed unchanged. This exactly fills the rectangular bounding-box perimeter while preserving marker cells.

Demo support: one demo had marker bbox rows 0–12, cols 3–8 and filled only gaps along the top/bottom rows and left/right columns; another had bbox rows 10–19, cols 2–22 and filled only its top/bottom horizontal and left/right vertical sides. This explains why unrestricted row/column interval filling fails: only extrema of the global marker bbox define active lines. Re-extract marker color and bbox each instance. Color 2 was the fill in observed demos. This accepted evidence supersedes the earlier unresolved-status note, while fresh layouts should still be validated against their demos.

## Additional accepted test (2026): task 8199b524

An 11×13 test with background 3 and marker 8 was solved with zero wrong attempts. The global marker bounding box was rows 1–6, columns 4–10 (0-based). Fill every background cell on this rectangle's perimeter with 2, preserving existing 8s and all cells not on that perimeter. Exact additions:
- top row r1: c6, c8
- bottom row r6: c5, c6, c8
- left side c4: r2, r3
- right side c10: r3
No other cells changed. This confirms the bbox-perimeter rule on another layout, including a multi-cell interior and short vertical side gaps. Continue extracting bbox from current marker locations and using fill color 2.

## Additional accepted test (2026): 12×18 instance

A test with background 8 and marker 4 was solved with zero wrong attempts. The global marker bounding box was rows 2–10 and columns 6–13 (0-based). Recolored only background cells on this bounding-box perimeter to 2, preserving marker cells and all non-perimeter cells. Exact additions:
- top row r2: c7–11 and c13
- bottom row r10: c7–11
- left side c6: r3–4 and r6
- right side c13: r5–7 and r9
No other cells changed. This directly confirms the bbox-perimeter rule with a full-width horizontal top/bottom bridge and selective vertical side cells.

## Additional accepted test (2026): 11×15 instance

An 11×15 test with background 9 and marker 8 was solved after one incorrect submission. The marker bounding box was rows 1–9 and columns 1–14 (0-based). The output fills only background cells on this rectangle's perimeter with 2; all existing 8s and all other cells remain unchanged. Exact additions:
- top row r1: c4, c6, c12–13
- bottom row r9: no additions (the two bbox corners c1 and c14 were already marker 8)
- left side c1: r3 and r5
- right side c14: r7

Important pitfall from the failed first answer: changing an existing marker on the bbox perimeter to 2 is wrong. Preserve marker cells even on the perimeter. Also do not add c2 on the bottom row: perimeter means only the bbox boundary columns c1/c14 on the max row, not every cell in the row.

## Additional accepted test (2026): 20×24 instance

A test with background 7 and marker 0 was solved with zero wrong attempts. The global marker bounding box was rows 4–10 and columns 15–23 (0-based). Output changed only background cells on this bbox perimeter to 2, preserving all marker 0s and all other background cells. Exact additions:
- top row r4: c17
- bottom row r10: none (the full segment c15–23 was already marker 0)
- left side c15: r7
- right side c23: r8

This further confirms the global marker-bbox perimeter rule for sparse side gaps with an already-complete bottom edge.

## Practical strategy

1. Identify foreground and decompose it into horizontal/vertical runs and components.
2. Compare exact deltas in every demo: selected and untouched gaps, orientation, run lengths, gap length, object/component membership, and whether endpoints are short strokes or enclosing boundaries.
3. Form a narrow selector before generating output; “collinear” alone is insufficient.
4. For the confirmed test above, the listed coordinates are exact, but do not transplant them to fresh layouts.
5. Validate dimensions and recolor only selected cells to 2; preserve all other marker/background cells.
